changes.evidenceEnglish: The three derivatives are distinguished by their attested forms. The tafsir of 56:37 treats أَتْرَاب as people of the same age.
The occurrence at 22:23:22 and its source gloss identify silk.
Al-Hajj 22:29:5 concerns fulfilling vows, a separate derivative from the warning verbs.
The sources on 22:28 include benefits of pilgrimage as a whole. The same noun is also used for livestock benefits.
At 22:28:20 the noun describes a person whom pilgrims are told to feed.
The contextual contrast at 22:25 is between the resident and the person coming from outside. The lexical derivative can refer to a person of the open country.
At 22:5:6, رَيْب is governed by فِي. Other occurrences use categorical negation.
At 22:5:64 the earth swells. The card also covers the other established meanings of the root.
Al-Waqi’ah 56:58 uses the Form IV reproductive sense. The recitation sense of Form V is recorded in the tafsir of 22:52.
